Add a per-function `is_dropped: [mut bool]` array (allocated/zeroed in `reset_ssa_tables` beside `is_global_addr`). When `has_drop == true`, allocate `block_dropped_out` (`func.blocks_len * ssa_count` bools, zeroed) and `block_visited` (`func.blocks_len` bools, zeroed); before each `check_block(block_ids[i])` call (both Pass 1 and Pass 2 `in_loop` blocks), clear `self.is_dropped[0..ssa_count]` to `false`, then for every block index `p` with `block_visited[p] == true` whose terminator (`ILInstr.Jmp(t)` or `ILInstr.Branch(br)`) targets `block_ids[i]`, OR `block_dropped_out[p * ssa_count + k]` into `self.is_dropped[k]`; after `check_block`, copy `self.is_dropped[0..ssa_count]` into `block_dropped_out[i * ssa_count .. In `mark_store`, only clear `self.is_dropped[base as usize] = false` (and reset `OwnerState.Owned`) when `self.is_stack_slot[base as usize]` or `!self.is_dropped[base as usize]`, so storing through a dropped heap `BoxMut` does not revive it.

Move `ILInstr.RegionCast(rc)` out of the default arm in `check_instr`, set `OwnerState.Owned`, propagate `points_to_stack` from `is_stack_slot[rc.val] || points_to_stack[rc.val]`, and propagate `is_global_addr` from `is_global_addr[rc.val]`.

- [x] +zil +safety +audit +AI-D @zil ZL6 Which common mistakes in hand-written ZIL zilc can catch from what ZIL says id:0mbg3
    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** the maintainer's decision in id:ahd1c (`future.tm.md`)
    > **Branch:** `zil`
    > **Depends:** id:egsdq, id:rvjcz, id:1dwwz, id:ks44a
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-21

    - **Placed:** after ZL5, which gives zilc the ZIL verifier this task extends.

    - **Why:** ZIL is not checked for memory safety, but zilc should catch the mistakes that are easy to see in ZIL as designed and that happen most often (the maintainer, id:ahd1c).
    - **Do:** list candidate checks, each with a three-line ZIL program that shows the mistake, and say for each whether ZIL as written carries what the check needs. Candidates to start from: a value used after a `move` or `drop` in the same function, a `drop` twice, a `slice_load`/`slice_store` with no dominating `bounds_check` (spec §6.3), the address of an `alloc 'local` returned or stored into a global, a `slice_len` or `slice_ptr` on a value that is not a slice, a `syscall` with an argument count its stub does not take, and a block with no terminator. Corpus mistakes count as evidence of what is common: id:1kaye's string over-read is one. Rank them by how often they would fire and how simple they are, and split each chosen check into an `+AI-G` task with its own numbered **Checks:** and a take-out.
    - **Checks:** C1: every candidate has its program and its answer here, with the zilc output today (`timeout -k 5s 30s build/zilc <file>`). C2: the chosen checks are tasks, placed after this one, with a check-in after them.
    - **Audit results (2026-11-21, `build/zilc` at `ad3b8c8`, cross-checked against `build/zoril --emit-zil` on `src/main.zrl` (538,925 lines: `slice_len=0 slice_ptr=0 slice_load=0 slice_store=0 bounds_check=0 move=11164 drop=0`), `tests/stdlib/test_stdlib_bufio.zrl` (30,182 lines: `unterminated=0 immut_store=1433 same_blk_uam=1`), and all 24 `corpus/zil/` files):**
      - **C1 — Candidate 1a/1b (use after `move` in the same function):**
        - Program 1a: `type T0: struct { x: i32 }; f0: i32 main() { @b0: v1: i32 = const 7; v2: T0 = struct_construct T0, v1; v3: T0 = move v2; v4: T0 = move v2; ret v1 }` -> `zilc` today: `exit=0` (no output).
        - Program 1b: `f0: i32 main() { @b0: v1: PtrMut<i32, 'local> = alloc 'local, i32; v2: i32 = const 7; store v1, v2; v3: PtrMut<i32, 'local> = move v1; v4: i32 = load v1; ret v4 }` -> `zilc` today: `exit=0`.
        - **Does ZIL carry what the check needs? NO.** ZIL has no `Copy` marker on types, and Zoril's lowerer emits `move` on stack slots of `Copy` aggregates and keeps reading fields from the slot in the same block (probed in `test_stdlib_bufio.zrl` at `@entry_2002`: `vbuf_13: Ptr<Slice<u8, 'local>, 'local> = move vbuf_5` followed by `v15: Ptr<u64, 'local> = field_addr vbuf_5, 1`). **Not chosen.**
      - **C1 — Candidate 1c & 2 (use after `drop` and double `drop`):**

- [x] +zil +decision +AI-D @zil ZL1 Settle the slice form of string_const and the slice_ptr opcode, and check what the pinned stage1 feeds zilc id:m6vm3
    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** the maintainer's decisions in id:1kaye (`future.tm.md`), 2026-11-13
    > **Branch:** `zil` (created off `main` at git:7c3b007)
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-21 git:7c3b007

    - **Placed:** after the provenance series (`id:z0017`), before ZL2 to ZL6. Nothing in `testinfra` depends on it. ZL4 changes the per-file runner, which `testinfra` rewrites (id:z0139).

    - **Depends changed (2026-11-17, a review of the task list, the maintainer's request):** removed id:z0017. It stated the order (this series after the provenance series), which the task's position states already; nothing in ZL1 to ZL6 needs a provenance task's result, and the series is on a branch of its own off `main`. `tm next` still offers the provenance tasks first; `tm next @zil` now offers this task, so a second session can take the series while the provenance series runs, if the maintainer wants that. To hold it back instead, restore the line.
    - **Why:** `string_const` is to give a `Slice<u8, 'local>` everywhere, as the spec says (id:1kaye, decision 1). Hand-written ZIL then needs `slice_ptr` to get the data pointer back.
    - **Decide, and write into ZL2 to ZL5 as their **Do:** and numbered **Checks:**:** (a) What a slice-typed `string_const` lowers to in zilc's QBE output: a static `{ptr, len}` pair beside the bytes, whose address is the value, or another layout. It must match how the front end's slice slots are laid out (pointer at offset 0, `usize` length at 8, today's `v5` slot in `--emit-zil`). (b) How the front end uses it: copy the pair into the slot, or use the value directly. (c) `slice_ptr`'s syntax, typing and spec entry beside `slice_len` (`doc/spec/intermediate_language.md` §5), and whether the front end's cast-and-load idiom is replaced by it. (d) What the pinned stage1 feeds to which zilc: does any path pass ZIL written by `bootstrap/stage1/` to the new `build/zilc`, `zilc-boot` included? If one does, the new zilc must also accept the old form until a re-pin, which is the maintainer's. (e) Which recorded figures change (`corpus/zrl_whole_program_zil.sha256`, the safety figures) and how each is recomputed.
    - **Also place:** the statement, decided in id:ahd1c, that ZIL is not checked for memory safety (`doc/spec/intermediate_language.md` and `doc/spec/safety_model.md`: the claims cover programs compiled from Zoril source, and zilc catches the common mistakes listed by ZL6). Put it into one of ZL2 to ZL5, or into a task of its own.
    - **Checks:** C1: each of (a) to (e) answered here, with the command that showed it for (d). C2: ZL2 to ZL5 each have a **Do:** and numbered **Checks:**, with a take-out check.
    - **Settled (2026-11-21):**
      - **(a) QBE lowering of slice-typed `string_const`:** in `tools/zilc/src/qbe.zrl`, `emit_string_data_sections` emits the NUL-terminated byte array `data $S<id> = { b ..., b 0 }` and immediately beside it a static 16-byte slice header `data $SS<id> = align 8 { l $S<id>, l <len> }` (pointer at offset 0, `usize` length at offset 8 — identical to every stack slice slot in ZIL/QBE). `IL_INSTR_STRING_CONST` emits `%vN =l copy $SS<id>` (and skips stack allocation in the entry-block aggregate-alloca loop at `qbe.zrl:1438`, which already excludes `IL_INSTR_STRING_CONST`). This makes `slice_len vN` (`loadl (vN + 8)`) and `slice_ptr vN` (`loadl vN`) work directly on `vN` with zero runtime initialization cost, and matches `is_aggregate(Slice)` where slice SSA values are 64-bit addresses of `{ptr, len}` pairs.
      - **(b) Front end lowering (`src/lower_zir_to_zil.zrl`):** `lower_rv_string_const` emits a single `vN: Slice<u8, 'local> = string_const "..."` and returns `vN` directly (no entry-block `alloc`, no `cast`, no two `store`s). Because `lower_stmt` marks `ZirRvalue.StringConst` in `local_owns` as non-owning (`aliases = true`, beside `Use`, `EnumPayload`, `GetEnv`) so `--checked` never poisons the read-only `$SS<id>` header at `EndBorrow`, and because `Let`/`Assign` into a non-tmp local already `memcpy`s 16 bytes from `val_ssa` into the local's stack slot (and `Ret` / `Call` pass the address of the `{ptr, len}` pair), using `vN` directly is both smaller and faster.
      - **(c) `slice_ptr` opcode:** add `IL_INSTR_SLICE_PTR = 73` and `ILInstr.SlicePtr(SSAId)` in `src/il_instr.zrl` (and handle it in `src/zil_print.zrl`, `src/il_typecheck.zrl`, `src/verify.zrl`, `tools/zilc/src/zil_parse.zrl`, and `tools/zilc/src/qbe.zrl`). Syntax: `vN: Ptr<T, 'local> = slice_ptr vS` (accepting `Slice<T, 'r>` or `Ptr<Slice<T, 'r>, 'r2>` as `vS`, and returning `Ptr<T, 'local>` / `RawPtr<T>`). QBE lowering: `%vN =l loadl %vS` (mirrors `slice_len`, which emits `add %vS, 8` then `loadl`). Document `slice_ptr` beside `slice_len` in `doc/spec/intermediate_language.md` §1, §5.6, and §7 (69 opcodes). Keep the front end's existing `load_slice_data_ptr` cast-and-load idiom unchanged for now (or optionally switch it in a later cleanup) so ZL2 stays minimal and focused; only `lower_rv_string_const` changes in front-end emission.
      - **(d) What pinned `stage1` feeds to which `zilc`:** checked via `grep -rn "build/zoril-stage1" Makefile scripts/` (and `scripts/bootstrap_zoril.sh`, `scripts/selfhost-check.sh`). Every invocation of `build/zoril-stage1` pairs it exclusively with `build/zilc-stage1`: (1) `Makefile:185-186` (`build/zilc-boot` runs `./build/zoril-stage1 ... --emit-zil` -> `./build/zilc-stage1`); (2) `scripts/bootstrap_zoril.sh:41-48` (`cc=build/zoril-stage1`, `zc=build/zilc-stage1`); (3) `scripts/selfhost-check.sh:174` (`generation ./build/zoril-stage1 ... build/zilc-stage1`). No path passes ZIL written by `bootstrap/stage1/` to the new `build/zilc` or `build/zilc-boot`. Therefore the new `zilc` does **not** need backward compatibility with pointer-typed `string_const`; `string_const` has one form (`Slice<u8, 'local>`) everywhere.
      - **(e) Recorded figures that change:** `corpus/zrl_whole_program_zil.sha256` changes in ZL2 because `lower_rv_string_const` emits `vN: Slice<u8, 'local> = string_const "..."` instead of the `alloc` + `cast` + `store` sequence; recompute with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 sh scripts/test_incremental.sh` in ZL2. Milestone safety figures (`bench/safety_matrix/README.md`) are not updated per task (`AGENTS.md` "Milestone figures are refreshed only at milestones"). The `fuzz-fresh` record becomes stale for `src/` and `tools/zilc/` (noted in ZL2/ZL3/ZL5 completion notes; renewed in `id:v2f8h`).
      - **Placement of the `id:ahd1c` safety-scope statement:** placed in ZL5 (`id:egsdq`), which wires `src/verify.zrl` into `zilc` and updates `doc/spec/intermediate_language.md` and `doc/spec/safety_model.md` to state clearly that Zoril's memory-safety claims cover programs compiled from Zoril source, while hand-written ZIL is checked by `zilc`'s type check and ZIL verifier (plus the common-mistake checks of ZL6), not for full memory safety.
      - **Checks answered:** C1: (a)-(e) answered above with `grep -rn "build/zoril-stage1" Makefile scripts/` for (d). C2: ZL2 (`id:qpc8d`), ZL3 (`id:htrqb`), ZL4 (`id:ehh6m`), and ZL5 (`id:egsdq`) updated below with concrete **Do:** and numbered **Checks:** including take-out checks.

- [x] +diagnosis +AI-D @main Two stage0c gates race on `build/zoril-c` in `make test` (`mv: cannot stat build/zoril-c.tmp`) id:nf1fv
    > **Created:** 2026-11-13
    > **Context:** found while doing id:z0136, which it did not cause.
    > **Branch:** `main`
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-21 git:7c3b007

    - **Promoted (main, 2026-11-20, the maintainer's request):** from `future.tm.md` for the next release, last of the `main` `+AI-D` group, before the `@zil` series. Retagged `@main`: the race is in `make test`'s stage0c gates, which a release's tarball check runs, not in the `testinfra` series.
    - **Placed:** future file, under Evidence and tooling: not blocking, and not a one-session fix until the cause is known.

    - **Seen:** `./scripts/test.sh --gates` failed `stage0c-corpus` (and once `stage0c-error-locations`) with `exited 2 without reporting a failing item`, in two of five runs on one host. `build/gates/stage0c-corpus.log` ends `mv: cannot stat 'build/zoril-c.tmp': No such file or directory` and `make: *** [Makefile:122: build/zoril-c] Error 1`. Both gates run `make -C bootstrap/stage0-c test_*` at once, and both can decide `build/zoril-c` needs rebuilding.
    - **Next:** read `bootstrap/stage0-c/Makefile` around line 122 and find whether the rule writes `build/zoril-c.tmp` under one name for every make; a rebuilt-once step before the gates start (or a per-process temporary name) would end it. The stage0 compiler is frozen except for a blocking bug, but the freeze covers the compiler, not its Makefile; ask the maintainer if a change there is needed.
    - **Diagnosed (2026-11-21):**
      - **Root cause 1 (`bootstrap/stage0-c/Makefile` line 122):** `$(TARGET_BIN): $(OBJS)` runs `@$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) $^ -o $@.tmp && mv -f $@.tmp $@` with a shared `build/zoril-c.tmp` name instead of a per-process `$@.tmp.$$$$` (unlike `$(VERSION_H)` at line 110, which already uses `$@.tmp.$$$$`). When two parallel `make -C bootstrap/stage0-c test_*` invocations (from `stage0c-unit`, `stage0c-corpus`, `stage0c-docs`, `stage0c-error-locations`, `stage0c-functional` in `scripts/test.sh --gates`) both decide `build/zoril-c` is out of date, both link `build/zoril-c.tmp` and the second `mv -f build/zoril-c.tmp build/zoril-c` fails with `mv: cannot stat 'build/zoril-c.tmp': No such file or directory`.
      - **Root cause 2 (why parallel gates decide `build/zoril-c` is out of date):** first, `./scripts/test.sh --gates` invoked directly (without `make test`'s `stage0c-build` prerequisite) starts all five `stage0c-*` gates in parallel with no prior `stage0c-build`. Second, even after `stage0c-build`, `bootstrap/stage0-c/Makefile` line 27 computes `VERSION_STR := $(shell ... sh ../../scripts/version.sh ../..)` on every `make` invocation, which runs `git -C ../.. describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --dirty`; if the working tree transitions between clean and dirty, `$(VERSION_H): FORCE` updates `build/version.h`, causing all five parallel `stage0c-*` gates to recompile `zoril-c.o` (racing on `build/obj/cc/no_san/zoril-c.o`) and relink `build/zoril-c` (racing on `build/zoril-c.tmp`).
      - **Fix (approved by maintainer 2026-11-21, git:7c3b007):** updated `bootstrap/stage0-c/Makefile` to use per-process `$@.tmp.$$$$` for `$(TARGET_BIN)`, `$(OBJ_DIR)/%.o` (with `-MF $(@:.o=.d.tmp.$$$$) -MT $@`), `cproc`, `minimal`, and `$(BUILD_DIR)/bin/*`; and updated `scripts/test.sh` to build `$STAGE0_DIR` once before dispatching the worker pool whenever any `stage0c-*` gate is in the plan.
      - **Verification:** deleted `bootstrap/stage0-c/build/zoril-c` and `zoril-c.o`, then ran all 7 `stage0c-*` gates in parallel via `./scripts/test.sh --quiet --gate stage0c-fixed-bugs --gate stage0c-unit --gate stage0c-corpus --gate stage0c-docs --gate stage0c-error-locations --gate stage0c-functional --gate stage0c-minimal`: `Total: 408 run, 408 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (25.6s)`. Ran `make test-changed BASE=HEAD`: `Total: 4134 run, 4134 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (147.4s)`.

- [x] +generics +types +AI-G @main id:z0032 G1 `impl<T: Copy> Source<T> for S` fails to bind `T` when it appears only in the trait's arguments
    > **Created:** 2026-11-03
    > **Context:** Rejected in both build modes.
    > **Branch:** `main`
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-21 git:100e5ac

    - **Promoted (main, 2026-11-20, the maintainer's request):** from `future.tm.md` for the next release, first of the `main` `+AI-G` group that follows the merge of `provenance` (id:w3vde); order inside the group is not critical.
    - **Reproducer:** `trait Source<T> { fn pull(self: &Self, fallback: T) -> T; } struct S { x: i32 } impl<T: Copy> Source<T> for S { fn pull(self: &S, fallback: T) -> T { return fallback; } } fn main() -> i32 { let s = S { x: 1 }; return s.pull(42) - 42; }` gives `type mismatch: expected &S, found bool`.
    - **Cause:** `impl_scope` (`src/mono.zrl`) binds an `impl`'s type parameters only by matching its target type. **Direction:** unify the trait's type arguments to bind the rest, mangle the bound arguments into the method name, and reject a parameter that appears in neither at the `impl` header.
    - **Checks recorded (2026-11-21, git:100e5ac):**

    > **Depends:** id:3nrvs

    - **Promoted (main, 2026-11-20, the maintainer's request):** from `future.tm.md` for the next release, first of the `main` `+AI-D` group after the `+AI-G` group; order inside the group is not critical. Re-probe against id:z0176's arm-scope change first.
    - **Placed:** in `future.tm.md`: a false refusal (the safe side), no task depends on it; after id:z0176's fix, whose arm-scope change it should be re-probed against.

    - **Found (`main` at git:8d4670b, `S: Drop`):** each is refused with `use of moved value`, though it moves each value once: `let (s, k) = t;` with `t: (S, i32)`, `let W { s: s, k: k } = w;` with `struct W { s: S, k: i32 }`, `match w { W { s: s, k: k } => .. }`, and `T.A((s, k))` for `enum T { A((S, i32)), B }` (`use of moved value 'the value of the expression at ..'`). Binding the aggregate whole (`T.A(t)`, `F.A(w)`) is accepted.
    - **Do:** find which move the checker sees twice (the destructured place, then a field of it), and accept a pattern whose bindings move disjoint parts; the rejection differential lists every newly accepted program, each read for a second owner.
    - **Done (2026-11-21, git:d94fe3b):**
      - **Cause:** `bind_pattern_name` (`src/lower_zir/lower_match.zrl`) emitted `ZirStmt.Let(local_id, ZirRvalue.Use(place), span)`, and `check_let` -> `check_rvalue_use` -> `check_place_use` (`src/check_zir.zrl`) treated every `ZirRvalue.Use(place)` as a full move of `place.base` (`state.ownership[place.base] = OWN_MOVED`) whenever `!loc.is_copy` (`S: Drop` makes the enclosing tuple or struct non-`Copy`). That marked the scrutinee local (or enum payload pointer temporary) `OWN_MOVED` at the first non-`Copy` binding, before subsequent sub-patterns in `lower_pattern_seq` (even a `Copy` sibling like `k: i32`) or subsequent `match` arms could read their parts. In addition, `lower_pattern_seq` and `lower_pattern_struct` noted skipped parts (`note_skipped`, which borrows `place` into a `LOCAL_KIND_LETMUT` pointer local) up front before testing sub-patterns and never emitted `EndBorrow` on those pointer locals when an `or`-pattern alternative failed or after `emit_skipped_drops`.
      - **Fix:** added `Local.is_pattern_binding` (`src/zir.zrl`), set by `bind_pattern_name` on by-value pattern bindings, and `check_place_move_allowed` (`src/check_zir.zrl`) so `check_let` checks that the projected part's place is initialized, not moved/dropped, not mutably borrowed, and allowed to move (not through a borrow, closure capture, or index, and not borrowed by another live local), while leaving `state.ownership[place.base]` owned until the whole pattern matches and emits `consume_place` (`check_places_consumed`). Moved `note_skipped` in `lower_pattern_seq` and `lower_pattern_struct` (`..`) onto the matching path, emitted `EndBorrow` on skipped-part pointer locals in `emit_skipped_drops` and on `pat_alt_fail`, and added checks in `lower_pattern_struct` and `bind_pattern_name` refusing duplicate struct pattern fields (`struct pattern names a field twice: <name>`) and duplicate binding names in the same pattern alternative (`identifier bound more than once in the same pattern: <name>`).

- [x] +safety +design +AI-D @provenance A call result tied through a reference to an owner holds what the owner holds, not the storage it owns, unless its type can point there id:sjqmy
    > **Created:** 2026-11-17
    > **Branch:** `provenance`
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-20 git:824841e

    - **Found by:** id:z0084, reading the reproducers P1 to P5 that the check-in id:n177h placed on it (`build/provenance/build/z84/p1.zrl`-`p5.zrl`).
    - **Placed:** directly before id:z0065, which it blocks (P1 to P4 are safe user code the default flip would refuse), and added to its **Depends:**.
    - **Now (compiler git:dadd49e):** P1 (`return v.clone()` of a local `Vec<u8>`), P2 (`Vec<[u8]>` holding a parameter's view), P3 (`String`) are refused by the return rule, which reads only `O`: the clone's result is `_8 O={Frame(_1)}`, `_1` the local `Vec`'s buffer. `Clone for Vec` reads `self.raw` and the elements through `self`, so its summary ties the result to `ParamContents(0)`, and the caller maps that to everything `&v` reaches through (`os_through_plus`), which includes `S(v)`, the buffer. `v.as_slice()` has the same summary bit and must keep `S(v)` (`build/z84/u1.zrl`: `return v.as_slice()` of a local `Vec`). P4 (`out.resize(1, v)`) is refused inside `stdlib/vec.zrl`'s `resize` (`value.clone()` of a by-value parameter, whose storage is `Frame(value)`) and at the call.
    - **Measured (a scratch compiler, not a rule):** in `os_call`'s `in_ties` branch, reading the tie through one level and keeping only what the pointee holds (`os_through_split` into `O`, its `S` dropped) makes P1 to P4 accepted and leaves P5's `c.push(&buf)` refused; it also accepts `build/z84/u1.zrl`, so as it stands it is unsound. The field-insensitive summary cannot tell `self.raw` (what the owner holds) from `self.data` (the storage it owns).
    - **Decide:** how a summary or the caller tells the two apart. Candidates: (a) a summary bit per parameter for "the storage what the parameter reaches owns" beside `ParamContents` (a read of an owner's own raw pointer field through the parameter gives it; `.zri` and edges carry it); (b) at the caller, leave `S` of the pointee out of a tie when the result's type can hold no pointer to anything the pointee's owned storage holds in place (`Vec<u8>` cannot point at a `u8` buffer except through its own `data`, which points into its own storage; `Vec<&u8>` can); (c) accept P1 to P3 as a bound, with a rewrite. Probe each against `u1.zrl`, `vec_clone_frame_views_returned_refused.zrl` (refused today for this reason, not for its views: id:z0084's **Consequence** bullet), `fn wrap(v: &Vec<i32>) -> Vec<[i32]>` pushing `v.as_slice()`, and a `Vec<Arena>` whose arena lies in the buffer.
    - **P5** (`c = v.clone(); c.push(&buf); return c;` with `v: &Vec<[u8]>`): the push is refused by the call store rule because `c`'s storage is the caller's arena (`ParamContents(0)`), which the design treats as external (§3, _Calls through a `fn` value_: "a frame view pushed into such a `Vec` built from a parameter's `fn` value is refused"). The buffer is fresh, and only `c` reaches it, so the stored view is unreachable once `c` is gone; whether that is accepted is part of the decision (id:n177h expected only the return rule). The `return c` refusal stays.
    - **Checks:** C1 the decision and its reason in the design note §3. C2 P1 to P4 accepted (or the bound and its rewrite in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` §5, written by id:z0065), `u1.zrl` and `vec_clone_frame_views_returned_refused.zrl` refused; with `v.push(&buf)` taken out of the latter, accepted. C3 the siblings above probed, each with a test. C4 the store grid under `--provenance`, `make test`, `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`.

    - **Related work parked (2026-11-18, id:bfd1z):** candidate (a) above is close to the `ParamOwned` word id:bfd1z built and measured. That word is a subset of ParamContents, written by an owning read (a raw pointer, a box, a 64-bit integer, a type parameter) and cleared by a read of a reference or a slice. It was not committed, because a held tie would free only 5 of the 84 declaration sites. Its patch against git:cd7e10d (**Patch: the word**), checks C1 to C4 and Findings A to C are in id:bfd1z's text in `completed.tm.md`. Finding A matters here: integers must stay owning reads, since a plain `as` cast makes a pointer with no Raw origin. The word gives the summary what this task needs, but no rule reads it yet. Here it would be read at the caller, in `os_call`'s tie arm: leave out `S` of the pointee where the callee's tie has no ParamOwned. Measure P1 to P5 and `u1.zrl` with the patch applied before choosing between (a), (b) and (c).
    - **Analysis (2026-11-20, on `git:7564798`, awaiting maintainer decision):**
      - **Current behavior of P1–P5 and `u1.zrl`:** since `id:mztqb` (`4241f2c`, `cd7e10d`, 2026-11-18) dropped `#[borrows()]` from `Clone for Vec<T>` and `Clone for String`, P1, P2, and P3 are **already refused in the default build** by the borrow checker (`cannot return 'v' a reference into storage owned by this frame...`) as well as under `--provenance` (`return rule`). P4 (`out.resize(1, v)` with `v: Vec<[u8]>`) is the only one accepted in the default build and refused under `--provenance` (`stdlib/vec.zrl:399:22` store rule + `p4.zrl:4:85` call store rule); 0 `.resize()` calls in `src/`, `stdlib/`, `tools/`, or `tests/` pass an owning `T` (all pass scalars or non-owning structs, and `423_resize_clones_drop_type_accepted.zrl` / `clone_returned_accepted.zrl` pass under `--provenance`). P5 is refused in both modes (`c.push(&buf)` is a real arena escape when `v` is arena-backed, since `v.clone()` reuses `v.raw_arena()`). `u1.zrl` is refused in both modes.
      - **Candidate (a) (`ParamOwned` / `ret_held`):** `id:bfd1z`'s inferred word alone does **not** fire on `Clone for Vec<T>` or `Clone for String` (`stdlib/clone.zrl`), because both contain `unsafe` blocks and call `self.raw_arena()` (`*mut ArenaHeader`), setting `os_ret_owned` to all-1s (`os_ret_held == 0`). Making (a) work on `Clone` requires H2 (`id:42ae2`: `#[unsafe(borrows(*self))]`) + H3 (`id:mqh84`: borrow checker reading `ret_held`), which the maintainer deferred to `future.tm.md` after `id:z0012` on 2026-11-18.
      - **Candidate (b) (caller type-based `S`-drop):** cannot make P1–P3 compile while the borrow checker keeps `self` borrowed until H2+H3; only frees P4 (0 callers in the tree), and is fragile on `Vec<Arena>` (returned `Vec`'s `arena: *mut ArenaHeader` can point into `v`'s buffer) and `Vec<T>`'s raw `data: *mut T`.
      - **Recommendation — Candidate (c):** document P1–P4 as a known bound in `doc/design/provenance.md` §3 and `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` §5 (with rewrites: move directly / `clone_in(&arena)` / push loop) until H2+H3 (`id:42ae2`, `id:mqh84`) resume after `id:z0012` (where `os_call`'s tie arm reads `ret_held` alongside H3's borrow-checker change). Keep P5's `c.push(&buf)` and `return c` both refused. Add the sibling tests (`u1.zrl`, `wrap(v: &Vec<i32>) -> Vec<[i32]>`, `Vec<Arena>`, `vec_clone_frame_views_returned_refused.zrl`) and close `id:sjqmy`.
    - **Checks recorded (2026-11-20, maintainer approved Candidate (c), git:824841e):**

- [x] +safety +tests +AI-D @provenance A `fn` item or closure that stores its own parameter into a global, made into a value, is refused by the new rules id:4f0ew
    > **Created:** 2026-11-17
    > **Branch:** `provenance`
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-20 git:3d15582

    - **Found by:** id:4by24, probing the sibling routes of a call through a `fn` value (compiler git:94c0ed2, and the same with id:4by24's change).
    - **Placed:** directly before id:z0012, which it blocks: once the old rules are deleted, both programs below compile and leave a dangling pointer in `G`.
    - **Now:** under `--provenance` the new rules accept both of these; only the old rules refuse them ("region escape: the function stores a reference into memory that outlives a call through a `fn` value"). A call through a `fn` value checks each argument against what the other arguments and the environment reach, never against a global (design note §3, _Calls through a `fn` value_), and the closure rule (id:z0096) applies only the edges whose value is what the environment reaches. An edge whose value is a declared parameter is checked nowhere.
      - `static mut G: *i32 = 0 as *i32; fn stash(r: &i32) { unsafe { G = r as *i32; } } fn apply(f: fn(&i32), r: &i32) { f(r); } fn bad() -> i32 { let x = 1; apply(stash, &x); return 0; } fn main() -> i32 { let _ = bad(); return unsafe { *G }; }` (a `fn` item; id:z0012's **From id:z0092** bullet names this half).
      - The same with `apply(|q: &i32| { unsafe { G = q as *i32; } }, &x);` in `bad` (a closure). The design note §3 _A closure made into a value_ said this one "is refused at `run`'s call"; no test showed it, and it is not (id:4by24 corrected the sentence).
      - A `fn` item bound to a local and called through it is refused, by its summary (`let f: fn(&i32) = stash; let g = f; g(&x);`: "the callee stores an address of this frame into a global (call store rule)").
    - **Do:** decide where a parameter-to-global (or parameter-to-another-parameter) edge of a body made into a value is checked: where the value is made (refuse the edge outright, as `check_fn_value` does), or at every call through a `fn` value (a global destination for every argument, which refuses every frame address handed to a `fn` parameter). Then implement it, with the two programs above as tests, and probe the siblings: an `unsafe fn` value, a method value (`S::get`), a generic instance, a closure in a struct field, a `fn` value returned by a call, and an `extern fn` (declared `#[unsafe(stores(p -> static))]` or undeclared) made into a Zoril `fn(...)` value via `unsafe { keep }` and passed to a `fn` parameter (found by id:g764h: accepted under `--provenance` because `os_is_c_fn_ptr` is false for `fn(...)`).
    - **Also:** the header comment of `os_check_closure_value` (`src/check_zir.zrl`) says the same wrong thing as the design note did ("An edge whose value is a declared parameter is checked where the argument is passed"); correct it with the fix.
    - **Checks:** C1 both programs refused under `--provenance` by a `provenance:` diagnostic, with a test each. C2 each sibling probed, refused where unsafe, with a test. C3 the rejection differential (it removes no refusal unless the decision does), `make test`, `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`.
    - **Checks recorded (2026-11-20, git:3d15582):**
      - **Decision:** refuse parameter-to-global edges where the `fn` value is made (`os_check_fn_value`, `OS_RULE_FN_VALUE` on `ZirRvalue.FuncAddr`), while leaving parameter-to-parameter edges to `os_unknown_call` at call sites (refusing globals at call sites would reject every callback taking `&T`). Also refuse any undeclared address-taking `extern fn` (or declared `extern fn` with a `-> static` edge) made into a Zoril `fn` value (not `extern "C" fn`). Updated `os_check_closure_value`'s comment and `doc/design/provenance.md` §3. Updated `Driver::set_ice_context` (`src/driver/module.zrl`) to format into a process-lifetime static buffer (`ICE_NOTE_PTR`) so `driver_lower_fn_instance` carries no parameter-to-global edge when passed to `Monomorphizer::set_lowerer`.

    - **Reproducer (100% checked code, compiles and exits 92 under `--checked` reading poisoned stack memory):**
      `struct FnStoreH { p: &i32 } fn fn_store_put(h: &mut FnStoreH, p: &i32) { h.p = p; } fn main() -> i32 { let hx: i32 = 7; let mut hh = FnStoreH { p: &hx }; { let hn: i32 = 9; fn_store_put(&mut hh, &hn); } if *hh.p != 9 { return 92; } return 0; }` (also reproduces when `fn_store_put` is called through a `fn(&mut FnStoreH, &i32)` value).
    - **Root cause:** `give_arg_borrows_to_target` (`src/check_zir.zrl`) records the callee's store as a `release_only: true` borrow on `hh`, and `check_local_scope_end` (`src/check_zir.zrl:3298`) checks `((!b.release_only && !b.derived) || self.local_type_has_drop(local_id, locals))`, skipping `release_only` borrows when `hn: i32` has no `Drop` impl even though `hn`'s stack slot is released at block end. Naively dropping `!b.release_only` from line 3298 rejects slice locals passed by value (`tools/zbuild/src/manifest.zrl:106`, `src/mono.zrl:871`) because `give_arg_borrows_to_target`'s fallback records `derived: false` even for `[T]`/`&T` arguments whose backing storage is not the local's own stack slot.
    - **Do:** distinguish borrows of a local's own stack slot (`&hn` passed as a reference argument) from borrows of a slice/reference local's backing target in `give_arg_borrows_to_target` (or `check_local_scope_end`), reject both the direct-call and `fn`-value inner-block reproducers, add safety probes, and run `make test` and `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`.

In `give_arg_borrows_to_target`, distinguish `from_addr` (`ParamAddr`) from `from_contents` (`ParamContents`), track `direct_inner` through `by_ref` slice arguments (`StructLiteral(ILTYPE_SLICE)` / `Cast` to slice / `inherit_reborrow`), treat slice indexing (`Projection.Index` on `ILTYPE_SLICE`/pointer) as non-local in `borrowed_storage_is_local`, and use converged `os_ret_addr` in `inherit_rv_borrows` when `os_known` is true.

    > **Created:** 2026-11-03
    > **Branch:** `provenance`
    > **Depends:** id:z0012
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-20 git:a1d539f

    - **Depends note:** (do not edit `src/summary_pass.zrl` before id:z0012 retires it; close with id:z0012). Over-rejection, not a hole; related to id:z0017.

    - **Now:** a safe program that hands a callee a reference to a local struct, and stores what the callee returns, is accepted when the reference is written in the call (`take_ref(&c)`) and refused when it first goes through a `let`, an identity function or an `if`. The callee returns the view the struct holds (`c.v`), not a pointer into the struct; the checker reads the result as a pointer into the caller's stack frame. Error: "region escape: returning a pointer to local stack storage via sret".
    - **In the grid:** all 3402 safe twins of the `ref_let`, `ref_identity` and `ref_phi` carriers (1134 each; id:z0041) are refused, and every twin of `ref_direct` is accepted. They are in `bench/fuzz/store_grid_twin_rejections.txt`: `grep -E '__ref_(let|identity|phi)__' bench/fuzz/store_grid_twin_rejections.txt`.
    - **Reproducer** (checked on the compiler of this commit, and the compiler before id:z0007 refuses it too, so it is not caused by that change). With `let r = &c;` and `take_ref(r)` in `f`, it is refused; with `take_ref(&c)` and no `let`, it is accepted, builds with `scripts/build_zrl.sh`, and exits 0:

    ```zoril
    struct Carrier { v: [i32] }
    fn take_ref(c: &Carrier) -> [i32] { return c.v; }

    fn f(out: &mut [i32], view: [i32]) {
        let c = Carrier { v: view };
        let r = &c;
        *out = take_ref(r);
    }

    fn main() -> i32 {
        let data = [42, 0];
        let mut dest: [i32] = @slice(0 as *i32, 0);
        f(&mut dest, &data);
        return dest[0] - 42;
    }
    ```

    - **Same refusal, other forms:** `take_ref(id_ref(&c))` with `fn id_ref(c: &Carrier) -> &Carrier { return c; }`, and `let r = if pick() > 0 { &a } else { &b }; take_ref(r)` with two carriers `a` and `b` and `fn pick() -> i32 { return 1; }`.
    - **Do:** find where a reference that passed through a `let`, a call or a join stops being read as "the reference to `c`" and becomes "a pointer into `c`'s storage", so that the callee's result is tied to the whole frame. Fix it so `take_ref` is tied to what `c.v` points at, not to `c`. This makes the checker accept more, so run the rejection differential (`scripts/check_reject_diff.sh <base>`) and list every program the base rejects and the change accepts; none of the store grid's unsafe cells may become accepted. Move the three carriers' twins out of the twin record in the same commit, and add one of the forms above as an `accept` probe.

      - C4: the rejection differential (`scripts/check_reject_diff.sh <base>`): every program the base rejects and the change accepts, listed in the completion note with its reason; none unsafe.
      - C5: the `accept` probe under `bench/safety_matrix/probes/`, and `sh scripts/run_safety_matrix.sh` passing; quote its summary.
      - C6: `make test` and `make preflight-changed`, each `Total:` line quoted, citing id:z0012's commit on `main`.
    - **Finding (2026-11-03):** id:z0047's read-through rule (`os_through_plus` on reference arguments) already gives `got O={Param(1)} S={}` on all three forms (`tests/language/memory/origins/read_through_{ref,identity,phi}.zrl`), `src/verify.zrl` accepts them with zero errors, and the sole refusal (`src/summary_pass.zrl:716`, "region escape: returning a pointer to local stack storage via sret") comes from `InterprocSummaryPass`, which id:z0012 retires and deletes. Do not change `src/summary_pass.zrl` beforehand; close this task with id:z0012 once the 3402 twins leave `bench/fuzz/store_grid_twin_rejections.txt`, the `accept` probe is added, and the rejection differential is recorded, citing id:z0012's commit on `main`.

- [x] +safety +precision +AI-D @provenance H4 Declare Vec.empty_like with borrows(*self) and infer Clone for Vec<T> per T, so probe 307 is accepted id:yc4ad
    > **Created:** 2026-11-20
    > **Branch:** `provenance`
    > **Depends:** id:mqh84
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-20 git:7f9e595

    - **Placed:** after id:mqh84, from which it was split; before its check-in id:22qty.
    - **Why:** H2 could not add `Vec.empty_like` with `#[unsafe(borrows(*self))]`: `stdlib/vec.zrl` is in the stage1 closure and the pinned stage1 does not parse `*self` inside `borrows(..)` (`stdlib/vec.zrl:69:22: error: expected identifier, but found *`). Declaring the tie on the generic `Clone for Vec<T>` is unsound (a `T::clone` returning a view into its source buffer was accepted: `tests/language/memory/provenance/vec_clone_self_view_original_changed_refused.zrl` keeps it refused).
    - **Stop and ask:** a stage1 re-pin or backport that parses `borrows(*self)` is the maintainer's decision. Then: add `Vec.empty_like`, rewrite `Clone for Vec<T>` on it with no `unsafe`, flip probe 307 to `accept`, remove the `Vec` bound from `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` §5, and re-run id:mqh84's C1 to C4 (P2 and P3 stay refused).
    - **Finding (2026-11-20): no re-pin needed.** `stdlib/clone.zrl` is outside the stage1 closure (`build/zoril --emit-deps src/main.zrl ...` lists `vec.zrl` but not `clone.zrl`), so the declared helper is a private `vec_empty_like<T>(v: &Vec<T>)` with `#[unsafe(borrows(*v))]` there, not a `pub` `Vec.empty_like` in `vec.zrl` (no new public API). `os_ret_held` is already inferred per monomorphized instance (`--emit-origins` prints `my_clone_Tu8`); `Clone for Vec<T>`'s inferred tie was unheld only because its body had `unsafe` (`held_spoiled`).

    > **Created:** 2026-11-19

    - **Placed:** at the top of `active.tm.md` (before id:77rr6) and added to id:z0065's **Depends:**. A previous session completed id:bfcvm (`git:6f31511`), id:kqp9n (`git:1b479e4`), and id:z0044 (`git:e84200e`) out of order without stopping at the mandatory check-ins on id:kqp9n and id:z0044. A review of those three commits found six verified safe-code UAF bugs (all accepted in both default and `--provenance` modes) and four implementation/doc issues that should be resolved before building further `src/check_zir.zrl` changes on top.
    - **Six verified UAF bugs (all compile cleanly at `git:e84200e` in default and `--provenance` modes):**
      1. **`check_arg_release` early-returns when `found_ab` is true (`src/check_zir.zrl:3871-3908`, id:kqp9n):** passing `&mut h` where `struct Holder { vp: &mut Vec<i32> }` to `fn kill_holder(h: &mut Holder) { h.vp.free(); }` after `*out = v.as_slice()` sets `found_ab = true` for `ab.base == h`, skips the `OriginSets` reachability fallback, and misses `v` (SIGSEGV, exit 139). Fix: do not skip the `OriginSets` check when `found_ab` is true (or walk `OriginSets` whenever `origins` is present).
      2. **`os_unknown_call_effects` passes `include_contents = false` for the closure environment (`src/check_zir.zrl:8104-8106`, id:kqp9n):** in `fn run(f: fn()) { f(); }`, `os_unknown_arg` for `k == args.len` yields `ParamContents(0)`. Passing `include_contents = false` to `os_add_releases` drops `OS_W_CONTENTS`, giving `run` `os_releases == 0`. Calling `run(|| { v.free(); })` after `*out = v.as_slice()` compiles and crashes (SIGSEGV, exit 139). Fix: pass `true` for `include_contents` on `k == args.len` (or preserve `ParamContents` reached through the environment).
      3. **`is_borrowed_by_other` skips `b.release_only` borrows (`src/check_zir.zrl:796-798`, id:kqp9n):** directly contradicts `doc/design/provenance.md` §3.1 item 2 ("a move or whole overwrite of the owner"). After `put(&mut s, &v)`, `let mut v2 = v; v2.free(); return s[0];` (SIGSEGV, exit 139) and `let mut a2 = a; a2.reset(); return s[0];` (reads `0xA5` arena poison, exit 165) are both accepted. Fix: `is_borrowed_by_other` must conflict with `b.release_only` borrows on moves of owning types (or unconditionally on moves).
      4. **`apply_unknown_store_borrows` skips `j == i` (`src/check_zir.zrl:4329`, id:z0044):** for an unknown `fn` value whose callee is not external (`let f: fn(&mut Pair) = if c { store_self } else { noop }; f(&mut p);`), `if j != i` skips storing argument `i` into argument `i`, so `p.s = p.v.as_slice(); p.v.free(); return p.s[0];` compiles and crashes (SIGSEGV, exit 139). Fix: remove `if j != i` (allow `j == i` in `apply_unknown_store_borrows`).
      5. **`can_rel` filter in `os_unknown_call_effects` (`src/check_zir.zrl:8089-8101`) and `check_call_ptr_releases` (`src/check_zir.zrl:4034-4053`) misses structs/tuples/enums carrying `&mut`:** both check `is_mut_pointer_tag(tag) || os_owns(...)` instead of checking whether the type can hold a mutable handle (`OS_Q_HANDLE`) or owns storage. Passing `struct Wrap { v: &mut Vec<i32> }` by value to `fn run(f: fn(Wrap), w: Wrap) { f(w); }` sets `can_rel = false`, so `run(kill_wrap, Wrap { v: v })` after `*out = v.as_slice()` compiles and crashes (SIGSEGV, exit 139). Fix: include `os_type_has(..., OS_Q_HANDLE)` (and a matching `ZirVerifier` helper) in `can_rel`.
      6. **`os_add_releases` skips `O(id)` for owning locals (`src/check_zir.zrl:8031-8034`, id:kqp9n):** `if !os_owns(c, module, table, lty)` stops traversal through a local `Box`, `Vec`, or `Drop` struct that holds a `&mut Vec<i32>` or `&mut Arena`. Follow `O(id)` when `os_type_has(c, module, table, lty, OS_Q_HANDLE)` (as `os_dest_reach` does) instead of `!os_owns`.
    - **Review findings to address in the same pass:**
      - `check_call_ptr_releases` (`src/check_zir.zrl:4060`) skips `callee.projections.len > 0` for unknown callees (`known || callee.projections.len == 0`); remove that guard so a closure called from a struct field or tuple slot is still checked.
      - `reset_driver_scratch` (`src/driver/module.zrl:48-58`, id:kqp9n) silently duplicated `stdlib/mem_raw.zrl`'s `arena_reset` without `#[releases]` to work around field-insensitive `releases` on `Driver` without recording the cost in `doc/design/provenance.md` §3.1 or adding `// SAFETY:` comments at its call sites. Decide whether to keep it (with proper `// SAFETY:` comments and a measurement note in `doc/design/provenance.md` §3.1) or replace it with a cleaner mechanism.
      - `--emit-origins` (`src/driver/module.zrl:1284, 1386`, id:bfcvm) dropped the `source_file == self.target_source_file` filter, dumping every imported stdlib function; decide whether to restore the filter (and adjust `releases_vec_and_arena.zrl` to inspect local wrappers or a flag) or document the whole-module dump.
      - `bench/safety_matrix/README.md` class `(H)` (`#[borrows()], reset`) still lists `--provenance` as `accepted`, though `gap_44_borrows_attr_reset.zrl` is already refused under `--provenance`. Update that cell.
    - **Checks:**
      - C1: add a `compile_reject` probe or `tests/language/memory/` regression test for each of the six UAF bugs (bugs 1–6 above) and verify each is refused in both default and `--provenance` modes (and fails/crashes with its fix taken out).

    - **Do:** at a call, for each store edge `i -> j` of the callee's summary, every local whose `Frame` the destination reach of argument `j` has receives the borrows argument `i` carries. - [x] +safety +tests +AI-D @provenance L2a A call summary records which arguments the callee may release id:bfcvm
    > **Created:** 2026-11-17
    > **Branch:** `provenance`
    > **Depends:** id:dhded
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-19 git:6f31511

    - **Placed:** directly before id:kqp9n (L2), which it blocks: L2's release tier conflicts only with a release, and it learns of a release from this fact.
    - **Design:** `doc/design/provenance.md` §3.1, item 2 (git:bdfcac6). The summary gets one new fact, `releases i`: the callee may release storage argument `i` reaches. It is computed from bodies, as the store edges are. A body releases `i` when it calls a releasing primitive on memory whose origins include `ParamAddr(i)` or `ParamContents(i)`, or calls a function whose summary releases an argument carrying them. A call through a `fn` value with no known callee releases everything its arguments and environment reach.
    - **Decide first, and record here:** how the releasing primitives are marked. They are `zoril_allocator_free` (`stdlib/mem_raw.zrl`, the only call to it in `stdlib/` is `Vec.free`) and the arena's reset and free (`stdlib/mem.zrl`: find each body that ends an arena's allocations). Either a trusted attribute on those few bodyless or `unsafe` items, as `#[fresh]` is (§3, _Raw operations_), or something else the design note's rules allow; no list of names in the checker. An `extern` releases nothing unless it is marked.
    - **Do:** compute `releases` in the origin pass (every mode: `os_pass_pending` runs with the rules off by default), keep it through a recursive cycle's fixpoint, write it into the `.zri` beside the store edges, and print it with `--emit-origins` (`releases 0`). Nothing reads it yet, so no program's verdict changes.
    - **Checks:**
        - C1: golden tests under `tests/language/memory/origins/` whose `--emit-origins` shows `releases 0` for `Vec.free`, for each arena reset and free, for `fn kill(v: &mut Vec<i32>) { v.free(); }`, and for a two-level wrapper of `kill`; and no `releases` for `Vec.push` (growth keeps the old buffer: `Vec.grow_to` frees nothing), a getter, and `fn put(out: &mut [i32], v: &Vec<i32>) { *out = v.as_slice(); }`.
        - C2: a recursive pair, one member freeing its argument, where both members' summaries release it.
        - C3: a `.zri` round trip under `tests/modular/iface_attrs/`: a module's releasing function, imported, prints the same `releases` as when compiled whole-program.
        - C4: take the primitives' mark out and watch C1's `Vec.free` golden fail; take the cycle step out and watch C2 fail.
        - C5: no verdict changes: `make test` and `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`, quoting the `Total:` lines and `reject-diff: base verdicts: fresh (no cache)` with 0 newly accepted and 0 newly refused.
    - **Decision (2026-11-19):** a trusted attribute `#[releases]` on an `unsafe fn` or `extern fn` taking at least one raw-pointer parameter (`*T` or `*mut T`), checked for placement and parameter type in `src/parser/decl.zrl` as `#[fresh]` is (with stage1-compatible bare `#[releases]` syntax and ignored in `bootstrap/stage0-c/src/surface_parser_decl.c`). In `src/check_zir.zrl`, `os_decl_releases` seeds the released parameter bitmask with every raw-pointer parameter of a `#[releases]` declaration (bit 63 for 63 and later), `os_call` unions `os_decl_releases` with the body summary `f.os_releases` and adds `ParamAddr(i) | ParamContents(i)` reached from `O(arg_k) | S(arg_k)` (`os_reach_all`) for each released argument `k`, and `os_unknown_call_effects` adds `ParamAddr(i) | ParamContents(i)` reached by any argument or closure environment of an unknown `fn`-value call. Marked primitives: `zoril_allocator_free`, `arena_free` and `arena_reset` in `stdlib/mem_raw.zrl` (the backing primitives of `Vec::free`, `heap_free`, `Arena::drop`, `Arena::reset` and `Arena::reset_to`), plus `arena_free` in `stdlib/local_mem.zrl`. No function name list in the checker.

- [x] +safety +tests +AI-D @provenance B3c A safe function may not hide a store behind a bare `extern` or a raw-pointer write: it declares `#[stores(..)]` id:f81f3
    > **Created:** 2026-11-18
    > **Branch:** `provenance`
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-19 git:3dcc47a

    - **Split from:** id:z0011, whose **Blind spot** bullet (id:z0049's review) and **Added by id:z0073's decision** bullet (case B, the maintainer, 2026-11-14) describe one rule: a safe function may not hide a store behind an operation the checker cannot read. Split off because id:z0011's ties check and its 13 + 85 sites fill a session already. The task text there allows this ("If that count makes this task more than a session, split the rule into a task of its own directly after this one").
    - **Placed:** directly after id:z0011, as that bullet asks.
    - **Rule:** a safe function that passes a pointer derived from a parameter to an `extern` that declares no effect, or whose `unsafe` block writes a value that can hold a reference or a slice through a raw pointer (one it was given, or one an argument holds: `unsafe { *self.p = r; }`), must declare `#[stores(..)]` (or `#[borrows(..)]`) naming what it stores and where, or it is a compile error. The declaration is then a trusted claim (`doc/SAFETY.md` §4.2), and the caller applies the call store rule to it.
    - **Probes:** id:z0060's reproducer with id:z0060's fix taken out; `put` with and without the declaration (`build/z76/cx.zrl` in id:z0076's text); a caller passing `&x` of a local where `g` reaches outside the frame (refused once declared); the same store of a plain integer (no declaration needed).
    - **Found open (2026-11-18, at git:44d96ab):** the route is accepted by the default build and by `--provenance`, and escapes. `build/z11b/caseb.zrl`: `struct H { r: &i32 }`, `struct Slot { p: *mut &i32 }`, a safe `slot_of(h: &mut H) -> Slot { return Slot { p: &mut h.r as *mut &i32 }; }`, a safe `put(s: &Slot, r: &i32) { unsafe { *s.p = r; } }` with no `#[stores]`, `leak(h: &mut H)` doing `let local = 42; let s = slot_of(h); put(&s, &local);`, and `main` reading `*h.r` after `leak(&mut h)` and a call that reuses the stack. Compile rc=0 in both builds; `sh build/2sdmk/run.sh build/z11b/caseb.zrl` prints `exit 0` (`h.r` points into `leak`'s dead frame; 7 had it not escaped).     > **Created:** 2026-11-18
    > **Branch:** `provenance`
    > **Depends:** id:z0011
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-19 git:5d7dc13

    - **Decided by:** the maintainer, 2026-11-18 (id:z0011's decision 1; principles 3 and 4 of `doc/vision/why_zoril.md`): a call reads a trusted callee's declared `ret_ties` instead of its body ties, so the trust is stated once at the point of trust and the callers are checked against it.
    - **Placed:** directly after id:z0011, as that decision asks; before id:f81f3, which does not depend on it.
    - **Why:** `os_call` builds a call's result from the callee's body summary (`os_ret_addr`, `os_ret_contents`), so a function that returns a trusted callee's result is still tied to what the callee's body ties. Examples: `Args.next` returning `self.get(..)` (id:mztqb); `pattern_through_ref` (`src/lower_zir/lower_match.zrl`) through `append_projection`; many of the 25 lowerer marks of id:mrdtf, which only call `alloc_u32s` or `append_projection`. Each needed a mark of its own.
    - **Do:** in `os_call`'s tie arm, for a callee with `borrows_trusted`, take the result's ties from `ret_ties` (as a bodyless callee's are) instead of the body summary. The result's own storage (`ret_storage`) stays the body's. Then list the marks in `src/`, `tools/` and `stdlib/` that no longer carry weight (id:bfd1z's measurement scripts with the report patch), and remove each in a commit of its own that names it.
    - **Checks:** C1: before, `Args.next`'s mark taken out of a scratch stdlib is refused under `--provenance`; after, it is accepted. C2: a probe of a trusted callee whose declaration is a lie (it names less than its body really returns, and the caller lets the result outlive the omitted argument) is accepted, which is the cost of trust: the probe documents it and the `SAFETY` line is where it is reviewed. C3: with the change taken out, C1's caller is refused again. C4: `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`, listing every newly accepted program with its reason (this makes the checker accept more). C5: `make test`.

    +// The parameters FUNC's result may point into by its final body summary, as a call reads them
    +// (os_call): its ParamAddr ties, and its ParamContents ties unless the result holds only integers.
    +fn os_body_ties(c: &mut OriginSets, module: &ILModule, f: &ILFunction) -> u64 {
    +    if f.ret_ty == 0 as u32 || !os_carries(c, module, f.ret_ty) { return 0 as u64; }
    +    if !os_holds_pointer(module, f.ret_ty, 0 as usize) { return f.os_ret_addr; }
    +    return f.os_ret_addr | f.os_ret_contents;

    +// `#[borrows(..)]` and the `&self` default are checked against the body (§3, _Checked
    +// contracts_): a call's borrows (inherit_rv_borrows) and every importer read `ret_ties`, so a
    +// result tied in the body to a parameter `ret_ties` leaves out would end that borrow while the
    +// result still points into it. A declaration may be wider than the body, never narrower. A
    +// closure's ties are its environment's, which no declaration names. A rule of `--provenance`,
    +// beside the others until they are the default. Returns the refusals.
    +pub fn os_check_ties(c: &mut OriginSets, module: &ILModule, idx: usize, span: Span) -> u32 {
    +    let f = &module.functions[idx];
    +    if c.rules == PROVENANCE_OFF || f.from_interface || f.is_extern { return 0 as u32; }

    +        return 0 as u32;
    +    }
    +    // A borrow is held only by a value whose type can hold a reference (inherit_rv_borrows), so
    +    // an integer result or argument carries none, whatever address its bits may hold.
    +    if f.ret_ty != 0 as u32 && !module.type_holds_reference(f.ret_ty, 0 as usize) {
    +        return 0 as u32;
    +    }
    +    let missing = os_body_ties(c, module, f) & !f.ret_ties;
    +    if missing == 0 as u64 { return 0 as u32; }
    +    let base = if f.params_len > 0 as usize && f.param(0).name == c.sret_name {
    +        1 as usize
    +    } else {
    +        0 as usize
    +    };
    +    let mut i = 0 as usize;
    +    while i < 63 as usize {
    +        if (missing >> (i as u64)) & 1 as u64 != 0 as u64
    +            && i + base < f.params_len
    +            && module.type_holds_reference(f.param(i + base).ty, 0 as usize) {
    +            let name = c.table.lookup(f.param(i + base).name);
    +            diag_start(c.file, span, if c.rules == PROVENANCE_WARN { "warning" } else { "error" });
    +            eprint("provenance: ");
    +            if f.has_borrows {
    +                eprint("#[borrows(..)] leaves out '");
    +                eprint(name);
    +                eprint("', which the result may point into; ");
    +                eprint("a declaration may name more than the body returns, never less\n");
    +            } else if f.ret_ties == 1 as u64 && i != 0 as usize {
    +                eprint("the result may point into '");
    +                eprint(name);
    +                eprint("', which the `&self` default does not tie it to; add `#[borrows(self, ");
    +                eprint(name);
    +                eprint(")]`\n");
    +            } else {
    +                // A by-value `Self` or type parameter, whose declared type showed no reference.
    +                eprint("the result may point into '");
    +                eprint(name);
    +                eprint("', which the elision default does not tie it to; ");
    +                eprint("add `#[borrows(..)]` naming it\n");
    +            }
    +            return 1 as u32;
    +        }
    +        i = i + 1 as usize;
    +    }
    +    return 0 as u32;
    +}

Accepted by the old rules and by `--provenance` at `a1ea096`; the caller's pointer is left dangling once `keep` drops `b`. Only `403a092` refused the first form, through the edge kinds id:z0072 removes.
    - **Question:** the stored value is a raw pointer, dereferenced only in `unsafe`. id:z0063 decided that the new rules check a raw pointer's origins (`Raw` is exempt only as a value).     - **A sibling route (found in id:z0076, 2026-11-05):** an owner holding a raw pointer to memory outside the frame, whose safe method stores an argument through it (`put(self: &mut G, r: &i32) { unsafe { *self.p = r; } }` called with `&x`), is accepted in both modes: the destination reach does not follow a `*mut` an owner holds (`os_type_has` answers no for `RawPtrMut(x)` under `OS_Q_HANDLE`). Program in id:z0076's text (`build/z76/cx.zrl`). Decide it with this case: a raw pointer's target is the `unsafe` author's claim, or the call rule follows it.
    - **Two more sibling routes (found in id:z0076, 2026-11-06):** a frame address stored through the result of a `#[fresh]` function (`tests/language/memory/provenance/fresh_store_through_old_rule_refused.zrl`) or through a heap block from `zoril_allocator_alloc(null, ..)` (`heap_block_store_through_old_rule_refused.zrl`), the pointer then returned, or the block put into a global (`heap_block_into_global_old_rule_refused.zrl`): any destination of the pointer. Since id:z0076 the new rules accept all three: the result has no origins, so a store through it reaches nothing they follow, as with a raw pointer an owner holds. The old region rule refuses all three in every mode today. Decide them with the case above: if a dangling raw pointer is outside the guarantee, say so in `doc/spec/safety_model.md`; if not, the store through a raw pointer with no origins needs a target (the fresh storage of the local holding it, say) before id:z0012 removes the old rule.
    - **Promoted (2026-11-14, the maintainer's request):** from `future.tm.md` with the whole provenance series, in its order there, after the open soundness holes on `main` and before the ZIL series. The series' notes moved to **Sprint notes** ("The provenance series").
    - **Decided (the maintainer, 2026-11-14, in a review of the plan):** the three cases are decided apart. **A** (a raw pointer value left dangling: `keep(out, b)` copies `b.data` out and `b`'s `Drop` frees the block; the `BothPtr` twin): outside the guarantee. A raw pointer in checked code carries no promise about what it points to; the dereference is in `unsafe`, where the programmer checks, and the checker cannot know that an owner owns what its raw pointer field points to. **B** (a safe function whose `unsafe` block stores an argument through a raw pointer an owner holds: `put(self: &mut G, r: &i32) { unsafe { *self.p = r; } }`): outside the guarantee as to inference, but the store may not go undeclared: such a function must carry `#[stores(..)]`, and its callers are then checked by the call rule. That rule is written into id:z0011, with the bare-`extern` rule already proposed there. **C** (a frame address stored through a `#[fresh]` result or a heap block that then leaves the frame): decided by a measurement, id:71a06, before id:z0012 deletes the old rule that refuses it today.

Document it in `surface_syntax.md` §2.5/§7.2 and `unsafe_policy.md` (beside `#[borrows(..)]` and `#[fresh]` as a trusted claim).

C5: `make test`, `make preflight-changed`.

- [x] +safety +precision +AI-D @provenance A clone is tied to what the original points into, not to the original itself, so probe 307 is accepted again id:2sdmk
    > **Created:** 2026-11-18
    > **Branch:** `provenance`
    > **Completed:** 2026-11-18

    - **Placed:** directly after id:mztqb, as its follow-up.
    - **Found by:** id:mztqb (git:cd7e10d). With `Clone for Vec<T>`'s `#[borrows()]` removed (closing gap_77), the `&self` default ties a clone to `self`, so `let mut v2 = v1.clone(); v1.push(2);` is refused (`bench/safety_matrix/probes/307_clone_is_independent.zrl:13:5: error: cannot mutably borrow 'v1' while it is already borrowed`). Probe 307 was flipped from `accept` to `compile_reject` with the reason, under design principle 1 (`doc/vision/why_zoril.md`: a correct program may be refused while the analysis is imprecise). A trusted `#[unsafe(borrows())]` is not a way out: the clone holds what the elements hold (gap_77) and lives in the original's arena, so it must keep that arena borrowed across a reset.
    - **Decide:** how a result is tied to what a parameter points into (`ParamContents`) without holding the parameter itself borrowed for mutation, for the borrow checker's ties (`inherit_rv_borrows`), and whether the same change frees other results of the same shape (a `String` clone, `Option` clone). Name what a wrong acceptance would hide (a clone outliving an arena reset, a clone of frame views returned: gap_77) and give a planted case for each.
    - **Checks:** C1: probe 307 flipped back to `accept`, gap_77 and an arena-reset twin (`let c = v.clone(); a.reset(); c.len()` with `v` in `a`) still refused. C2: `sh scripts/run_safety_matrix.sh` with 0 mismatches. C3: `make test`, `REJECT_DIFF_NO_CACHE=1 make preflight-changed`, every newly accepted program listed with its reason.

C1 to C3 are H3's checks, where they are numbered again. This task is the decision; it stays open until the maintainer approves it, because it adds a new form of a trusted attribute and a `pub` stdlib method (see **Decision**).
    - **Finding 1, `ParamContents` alone is not enough (2026-11-18, `build/zoril` at git:cd7e10d, `build/2sdmk/shapes.zrl`):** `--emit-origins` gives the same return set for a view into the Vec's own buffer, a clone, and a copy of a stored slice: `fn sl(v: &Vec<u8>) -> [u8] { return v.as_slice(); }` `return O={ParamContents(0)} S={}`; `fn cl(v: &Vec<[u8]>) -> Vec<[u8]> { return v.clone(); }` `return O={ParamContents(0)} S={ParamContents(0)}`; `fn hd(v: &[u8]) -> [u8] { return *v; }` `return O={ParamContents(0)} S={}`. A read through `ParamAddr` or `ParamContents` memory yields `ParamContents` whatever it reads (`os_through`), so the sets do not record whether the memory is *owned* by the referent (the Vec's buffer, reached through the raw `data`) or only *borrowed* by it (its arena, its elements' referents). So the obvious rule, "a `ParamContents`-only tie inherits what the referent holds, not the referent", accepts a use after free: P1 below.
    - **Finding 2, the answer depends on `T` (same build, `build/2sdmk/selfref.zrl`):** a safe `Clone` may return a value pointing into its source. `struct S { a: [u8; 4], v: [u8] }` with `fn clone(self: &S) -> S { return S { a: self.a, v: &self.a }; }` is accepted and runs (exit 5). So `Vec<S>.clone()` points into `v1`'s buffer, and a trusted narrowing on the generic `Clone for Vec<T>` would be false for that `T` (principle 3 allows trust only where it is true): P2 below. Summaries are per instance (`Vec_Tu8::clone` and `Vec_TSu8::clone` are separate functions in the ZIL), so the answer can be computed per `T`.
    - **Finding 3, the trust has to sit on the arena pointer:** `Vec.clone` reaches its arena only through `self.raw_arena()`, a raw pointer read, and no body analysis can tell a raw field that owns (`data`) from one that borrows (`raw`). That is unsafe-interior knowledge, so it is a trusted declaration, but on a `T`-independent function whose claim is true for every `T`, not on the generic clone.
    - **Decision (proposed 2026-11-18, awaiting the maintainer):**
      1. _A new summary fact, `ret_held` (a mask beside `ret_ties`):_ bit `i` says the result points into what argument `i`'s referent *holds*, and into nothing the referent is or owns.
      2. _The caller (H3):_ in `inherit_rv_borrows`, for a tied argument whose bit is in `ret_held` and not in `ret_storage`, each *direct* borrow the argument carries (the `&v1` of the call) is replaced by the borrows the borrowed place's local holds (borrower = that local), copied with their own flags. The argument's other borrows are kept as they are today. So `v2 = v1.clone()` holds what `v1` holds (its arena, the views pushed into it) and not `v1`. A referent the checker records nothing for (a parameter of the caller, a place behind a pointer) keeps today's rule. This relies on the invariant the push and store rules already keep: what a local points into, other than its own and its owned storage, is held by it as a borrow (a view of its own buffer pushed into itself is a borrow of itself: P5).
      3. _The body (H1):_ the origin sets get a word `OS_W_OWNED` beside `OS_W_CONTENTS`, `ParamOwned(i)` ⊆ `ParamContents(i)`: the address may point into the referent of argument `i` or into storage it owns. The existing rules never read it, so the store and return rules do not change. A read (`os_through`) of a value whose type can own (a raw pointer, a box, anything holding one or a type parameter not yet known) carries `ParamAddr | ParamOwned` of the memory into `ParamOwned`; a read of a reference or a slice carries none (what a borrowing value stored in the referent points to is held by the referent, by the invariant of 2). Every other write of `ParamContents` (an unknown call, an `extern`, a cast, a call whose tie is not held) also writes `ParamOwned`: the word starts conservative and is cleared only by those two rules and by a held call (a callee's `ret_held` bit gives the result what is reached through the argument, without `ParamOwned`). `ret_held` = the bits of `ParamContents` in `O(ret)` and `S(ret)` with no `ParamAddr` and no `ParamOwned` in either. Only a body with no `unsafe` block, not an `unsafe fn`, and no call to an `extern` of its own gets an inferred `ret_held`: a copy through a bare `extern` or a raw write would hide an owned pointer from the sets (id:f81f3's blind spots). A recursive cycle's open callee is read as not held, as for ties.
      4. _The trust (H2):_ `#[unsafe(borrows(*self))]`, read "the result borrows what `*self` borrows", sets `ret_held` for `self` on a function whose body the inference cannot read. Two uses: a new `pub fn empty_like(self: &Vec<T>) -> Vec<T>` (an empty Vec allocating from the same arena, true for every `T`), so that `Clone for Vec<T>` becomes a safe body (`empty_like` then `push(get(i).clone())`) that H1 infers per `T`; and `Clone for String` directly (its bytes hold nothing; the arena is held). A plain `#[borrows(*self)]` (a checked contract) is left to id:z0011. The `.zri` carries `ret_held` as a `#[summary]` key, so an importer that finds none reads no held bit (the strict side).
      5. _What it frees besides probe 307:_ `[T].clone` and `Option<T>.clone` are inferred (a slice read through `self`; `v.clone()` of a held `T`), and so is every safe accessor returning a stored view (`fn name(self: &Tok) -> [u8] { return self.text; }`), which no longer keeps the struct borrowed. The rejection differential lists them; the `src/` sites it frees are expected and are listed, not judged one by one.
      - _Alternative not taken:_ §3.1's release tier (`doc/design/provenance.md`) would also accept probe 307 (`push` releases nothing). But L1 decided a borrow a call result holds keeps today's rule, and the release tier does not exist yet; the decision above keeps that rule and changes only which place is borrowed.
    - **Planted cases** (each refused by `build/zoril` at git:cd7e10d; the reproducers are in `build/2sdmk/`, the text below). Each is a numbered check of H1 or H3, with its safeguard taken out to show it can fail:
      - P1, a view into the original's own buffer (hides a use after free from the author of `v.as_slice()`; safeguard: `ParamOwned` from a raw read): `let mut v = Vec::<u8>.new(); v.push(7); let s = v.as_slice(); v.free(); return s[0] as i32;` refused, "cannot mutably borrow 'v' while it is already borrowed".
      - P2, a clone whose `T.clone` points into its source (hides a use after free from a user with such a `T`; safeguard: per-instance inference, no trust on the generic clone): `S` as in Finding 2, `let e = [9 as u8; 4]; let mut v1 = Vec::<S>.new(); v1.push(S { a: [5 as u8; 4], v: &e }); let v2 = v1.clone(); v1.free(); return v2.get(0).unwrap().v[0] as i32;` refused, "cannot mutably borrow 'v1' while it is already borrowed".
      - P3, the arena reset (hides a read of a reset arena; safeguard: the caller copies the referent's borrows): `let mut a = Arena.new(4096).unwrap(); let mut v = Vec::<u8>.new_in(&a); v.push(7); let c = v.clone(); a.reset(); return c.len() as i32;` refused, "cannot mutably borrow 'a' while it is already borrowed".
      - P4, gap_77 (a clone of frame views returned; safeguard: the copied borrows keep the escape rule's view of `buf`): refused, "cannot return 'v' ...". With the change the refusal names `buf` instead.
      - P5, views into the struct's own buffer stored in the same struct (hides a free under a held accessor; safeguard: the self-borrow is among the borrows copied): `struct T { buf: Vec<u8>, names: Vec<[u8]> }`, `fn first(t: &T) -> [u8] { return *t.names.get(0).unwrap(); }`, `t.buf.push(7); t.names.push(t.buf.as_slice()); let n = first(&t); t.buf.free(); return n[0] as i32;` refused, "cannot mutably borrow 't.buf' while it is already borrowed". (Line 10, the self-borrowing push, is accepted today.)
      - P6, an owned pointer hidden behind a bare `extern` copy in a safe-looking body (safeguard: no inference for a body with `unsafe` or an `extern` call): a function `fn leak(v: &Vec<u8>) -> [u8]` that copies `v`'s buffer pointer into its result through `memcpy` in an `unsafe` block, then `v.free()` while the result lives: refused. To write in H1.
      - P7, separate compilation (hides P2 and P3 from a `zbuild` user; safeguard: the `.zri` key): P2, P3 and probe 307 under `zbuild` agree with whole-program (`safety-matrix-zbuild`, `zbuild-diff`).
      - P8, a receiver that is not a direct borrow (`v.get(0).unwrap().clone()` for a `Vec<Vec<u8>>`, then `v.free()`): refused (the derived borrow of `v` is kept).
      - P9, a view a callee stored into the referent without a recorded borrow (gap_96's class; hides a use after free from any caller of a held function; safeguard: H3 waits for holders one to three): `struct T { buf: Vec<u8>, names: Vec<[u8]> }`, `fn index(t: &mut T) { t.names.push(t.buf.as_slice()); }`, `fn first(t: &T) -> [u8] { return *t.names.get(0).unwrap(); }`, then `t.buf.push(7); index(&mut t); let n = first(&t); t.buf.free(); return n[0] as i32;` is refused today ("cannot mutably borrow 't.buf' while it is already borrowed", the borrow of `t` at `first(&t)`). Without `first`, reading `t.names` after the free is accepted and faults (`build/2sdmk/p9_direct.zrl`, exit 139): `t` records no borrow of `t.buf`. So decision (2), which copies only `t`'s recorded borrows, would accept the first program, a new route into gap_96's class.

A reference, a slice or an aggregate made only of them gets none. `os_read` applies it with the value's type, and `os_walk` with the type of the pointer at each step (`&T` none, `*T` and a `Vec`'s buffer the owning read). That is H2's trusted shape (the arena is held), not inference. `src/fmt/doc.zrl:78` `cmd_at`: `self.cmds.as_slice()[i]` reads a `DocCmd` whose integer fields make it an owning read (Finding A). `src/lexer.zrl:241` `Lexer.text_from`: the length `(self.pos - start)` is an integer read through `self`, and `subslice` ties its result to it (Findings A and C).
      - _Upper bounds:_ variant L (Finding C) gives 6 held; variant I, integers as non-owning reads (unsound by Finding A; only a ceiling), gives 10 (L's 6 plus `fmt/doc.zrl:78`, `parser/decl.zrl:359`, `zil_parse.zrl:843` and the test's own `popped_integer_carries_no_address_accepted.zrl:13`).
    - **C7, the recommendation:** the count is small: 5 of the 84 `src/` and `tools/` sites (6 with Finding C, 10 at the unsound ceiling). 51 are `unsafe` bodies and 18 point into the referent itself, which a held tie cannot free whatever its rule. So by the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-18 (in id:2sdmk), id:42ae2, id:mqh84 and id:22qty move to `future.tm.md`, to resume after id:z0012, and the word is not committed. id:mrdtf goes ahead without them. Its five held sites, and `text_from` if Finding C lands, are the ones H2 and H3 would later free by inference; until then they are exemptions like the rest. When H2 resumes, it starts by applying the patch below, since H2's `ret_held` bit is this word's.
    - **Measurement scripts** (copy into `build/bfd1z/`, run from the repository root). `mk.sh SRCDIR OUT` builds a scratch compiler from a copy of `src/` with `build/zoril` (the `as` warning `0x8000000000000000 shortened to 0x0` it prints is in id:mztqb's scratch build too, not in `make`'s). `measure.sh ZORIL OUT` collects the `HELDSITE` lines; `bysite.sh OUT` groups them by `file:line`. For C6: `cp -r src build/bfd1z/src_m`, apply the word and the report patch there, `mk.sh build/bfd1z/src_m build/bfd1z/zoril.m`, `measure.sh build/bfd1z/zoril.m build/bfd1z/m`, `bysite.sh build/bfd1z/m`. Variants L and I are applied on top of `src_m`.
    ```sh
    # mk.sh
    S=$1; O=$2
    timeout -k 5s 300s build/zoril -I stdlib=stdlib -I "$S" -I build/gen --emit-zil -o "$O.zil" "$S/main.zrl" > "$O.log" 2>&1 || { echo "zoril failed"; tail -5 "$O.log"; exit 1; }
    timeout -k 5s 300s build/zilc "$O.zil" "$O.ssa" >> "$O.log" 2>&1 || { echo "zilc failed"; exit 1; }
    qbe -o "$O.s" "$O.ssa" && as -o "$O.o" "$O.s" && ld -o "$O" "$O.o" build/runtime.o || exit 1
    echo "built $O"
    # measure.sh
    Z=$1; O=$2; mkdir -p $O; : > $O/sites.txt
    for root in src/main.zrl tools/zilc/src/main.zrl tools/zbuild/src/main.zrl tools/zman/src/main.zrl tools/ztest/src/main.zrl; do
      timeout -k 5 300 $Z -I stdlib=stdlib -I $(dirname $root) -I src -I build/gen --emit-zil -o /dev/null $root > $O/root.log 2>&1
      echo "$root rc=$?" >> $O/roots_rc.txt
      grep HELDSITE $O/root.log | sed "s|^|ROOT $root: |" >> $O/sites.txt
    done
    while read -r tf; do
      fl=$(sed -n 's|^// flags: ||p' $tf | head -1)
      timeout -k 5 30 $Z -I stdlib=stdlib -I $(dirname $tf) $fl --emit-zil -o /dev/null $tf > /dev/null 2>$O/t.err
      grep HELDSITE $O/t.err | sed "s|^|TEST $tf: |" >> $O/sites.txt
    done < build/mztqb/m_base/tests_compiled.txt
    echo "$O $(grep -c '' $O/sites.txt)"
    # bysite.sh
    D=$1
    sed 's/^[A-Z]* [^ ]*: //' $D/sites.txt | sed 's/:\([0-9]*\):[0-9]*: warning: HELDSITE/:\1 /' | sort -u > $D/distinct.txt
    awk '{split($1,a,":"); site=a[1]":"a[2]; k=$2; st=($NF=="held=yes")?"held":$NF; key=site" "k; if(!(key in s)) {s[key]=st; order[++n]=key} else if (s[key]!=st && index(s[key],st)==0) s[key]=s[key]","st} END{for(i=1;i<=n;i++) print order[i], s[order[i]]}' $D/distinct.txt | sort > $D/bysite.txt
    ```
    - **Patch: the report** (`build/bfd1z/report.patch`, on top of the word; it prints a `HELDSITE` warning per site in any mode):
    ```diff
    --- a/src/check_zir.zrl	2026-11-18 21:00:14.931752854 +0000
    +++ b/src/check_zir.zrl	2026-11-18 21:03:10.155552509 +0000
    @@ -8449,8 +8449,61 @@
     // A body in a recursive cycle gets its ties once the cycle's summaries are final, after the
     // borrow checks of the cycle's own bodies ran; those read a call into the cycle as tied to every
     // argument instead (inherit_rv_borrows, ILFunction.os_in_cycle).
    +// Scratch (id:bfd1z measurement only): each result tie a declaration or the elision default
    +// leaves out, and whether it is held.
    +fn os_held_report(c: &mut OriginSets, module: &ILModule, f: &ILFunction) {
    +    if f.from_interface || f.is_extern { return; }
    +    if f.params_len > 0 as usize
    +        && type_name_is(c.table.lookup(f.param(f.params_len - 1 as usize).name), "__env") {
    +        return;
    +    }
    +    if f.ret_ty != 0 as u32 && !module.type_holds_reference(f.ret_ty, 0 as usize) { return; }
    +    let base = if f.params_len > 0 as usize && f.param(0).name == c.sret_name { 1 as usize } else { 0 as usize };
    +    let missing = os_body_ties(c, module, f) & !f.ret_ties;
    +    let mut i = 0 as usize;
    +    while i < 63 as usize {
    +        if (missing >> (i as u64)) & 1 as u64 != 0 as u64 && i + base < f.params_len
    +            && module.type_holds_reference(f.param(i + base).ty, 0 as usize) {
    +            let bit = (1 as u64) << (i as u64);
    +            diag_start(c.file, f.decl_span, "warning");
    +            eprint("HELDSITE ");
    +            eprint(if f.has_borrows { if f.borrows_trusted { "trusted" } else { "borrows" } } else { "default" });
    +            eprint(" fn=");
    +            eprint(c.table.lookup(f.name));
    +            eprint(" param=");
    +            eprint(c.table.lookup(f.param(i + base).name));
    +            if f.os_ret_held & bit != 0 as u64 {
    +                eprint(" held=yes\n");
    +            } else {
    +                eprint(" held=no reason=");
    +                let r = 2 as usize * c.nl;
    +                let o = r * c.words;
    +                let s = o + c.words;
    +                if c.held_spoiled {
    +                    eprint("unsafe-or-extern");
    +                } else if (c.buf[o + OS_W_FLAGS] | c.buf[s + OS_W_FLAGS]) & ORIGIN_UNKNOWN != 0 as u64 {
    +                    eprint("unknown-origin");
    +                } else if (c.buf[o + OS_W_FLAGS] | c.buf[s + OS_W_FLAGS]) & ORIGIN_RAW != 0 as u64 {
    +                    eprint("raw-origin");
    +                } else if f.os_ret_owned == 0xffffffffffffffff as u64 && f.os_in_cycle {
    +                    eprint("cycle");
    +                } else if f.os_ret_owned == 0xffffffffffffffff as u64 {
    +                    eprint("frame-or-earlier-pass");
    +                } else if (c.buf[o + OS_W_ADDR] | c.buf[s + OS_W_ADDR]) & bit != 0 as u64 {
    +                    eprint("param-addr");
    +                } else {
    +                    eprint("param-owned");
    +                }
    +                eprint("\n");
    +            }
    +        }
    +        i = i + 1 as usize;
    +    }
    +}
    +
     pub fn os_infer_ties(c: &mut OriginSets, module: &mut ILModule, idx: usize) {
